title: Scan state file state diagram
description: The life of one scan, as the state file records it: the meta table's cfg and finished keys and the dirs table's done flags. There is no Rust type for it; cmd_new, cmd_resume and run_scan drive it. Running and paused look the same on disk (directories still pending, no finished key); running means a process is walking them. compress and dedupe read a paused scan with a warning and do not change it.
machine: Scan state file (scan.rs: meta cfg and finished, dirs.done)

states.description: No state file at the path; status, list, resume, compress and dedupe exit with an error pointing at new.
A new or resume process takes the newest pending directory, records its entries, marks it done, and commits progress about every 2 seconds.
Directories are still pending and no process is walking them; progress up to the last commit is kept.
No directories pending; meta.finished holds the time it completed.

transitions.action: Create the database, store cfg and started, queue the root.
Queue subdirectories, record files and candidates, mark it done; commit stats and elapsed time when 2 seconds have passed.
Finish the current directory, commit, print Scan paused.

transitions.trigger: second Ctrl-C, or the process is killed
transitions.action: Exit at once; work since the last commit is lost and redone on resume.
Commit, set meta.finished, print the candidate total and the next steps.

transitions.guard: the meta table holds a scan configuration
transitions.action: Read cfg back and continue with the pending directories.
Refuse: an unfinished scan exists; use resume or new --force.
Delete the database and its WAL files, then start afresh.
Print that the scan is already complete.
Delete the database and its WAL files, then start afresh.
